Thursday, Google announced plans of rolling out “Tap to Translate” feature on Android smartphones, wipe out the cumbersome task of copy-paste routine whenever people need to get their text translated into other language.

With this upcoming feature, user will be able to choose the text of a chat, lyrics or comment of a song in whichever app user is using and right there a translation will pop up, ending the need to switch to other translation apps, Google said in a statement on Thursday. With Tap to Translate, improved Offline Mode, and Word Lens in Chinese, we hope you’ll find the latest version of Google Translate a helpful companion. These updates are rolling out over the next few days.

“Tap to Translate” will work for all 103 of the internet giant Translate’s languages on any Android phone operating on Jellybean (4.2) and higher. Another feature called “Offline Mode” now works on iOS platform and joins Android in using small offline packages.

Google has also added a Filipino language pack, bringing total number of offline languages to 52. With “Tap to Translate”, Google hopes to improve the Google Translate experience for users. The search engine giant has talked with thousands of people in India, Brazil, Indonesia and Thailand to learn exactly what works and what doesn’t—and on Thursday they rolled out some big improvements.
